basic_identification.full_title: Fish and Fishery Products — Sampling (मछली और मत्स्य उद्योग के उत्पादों के नमूने लेने की पद्धति) (First Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Food and Agriculture / Fish, Fisheries, and Aquaculture (approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council and finalized by the Fish, Fisheries, and Aquaculture Sectional Committee, FAD 12, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Fish, Fisheries, and Aquaculture Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies standard methods, scales of sampling, sample-size criteria, and criteria for conformity for sampling fresh, frozen, canned, dried, dry-salted fish, and other fishery products (including fish oils) to ensure representative, aseptic samples are drawn for physical, chemical, and microbiological examinations.

version_status_and_amendments.year_first_published: 1985 (originally published under the designator IS 11427 : 1985, and updated to first revision in 2001)
version_status_and_amendments.amendment_slips: No active amendments have been issued on this reaffirmed copy (NIL on this copy).

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: Methods for random sampling
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Establishes standard statistical procedures and random number tables to ensure unbiased sample selection from lots.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Code of Practice / Sampling and Inspection Guidelines (Food and Agriculture / Fish and Fisheries)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 11427 : 2001 is a statistical sampling methodology and inspection guideline rather than a direct consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp. However, compliance with its sampling scales, container quantities, and testing timelines is strictly mandated in public sector food supply contracts, state fishery department quality audits, import/export inspections (under the Export Inspection Council and EIA), and municipal food safety certifications (including FSSAI audits) across India to validate fish product quality and resolve contractual disputes. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: Cans or packages of the same type of pack containing material of the same variety, same grade, and packed at the same place on the same day shall constitute a lot.

requirements.requirement_type: Table 1: Scale of Sampling for Canned Fish / Cartons

requirements.detail: If sampling is done before packing into cartons, the equivalent number of cartons shall be computed based on 24 cans to a carton for packs up to 120 g, and 12 cans to a carton for packs larger than 120 g, after which Table 1 scales are applied.

requirements.requirement_type: Table 2: Selection of Containers for Fresh Fish
Table 4: Scale of Sampling for Dried and Dry-Salted Fish
Table 5: Scale of Sampling for Fish Oils

requirements.detail: From the selected packages of dried/salted fish, five (5) composite samples shall be drawn aseptically under sterile conditions using sterile knives, and transferred to sterilized, airtight containers.

requirements.requirement_type: Physical Sampling Methods for Fresh Fish

requirements.detail: Samples must be taken within three weeks of delivery, and all tests must be commenced within one week of sampling. If immediate testing is not possible, samples must be packed in airtight containers and tested within a maximum limit of three months.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 11427 : 2001 (First Revision) is the national Indian Standard specifying methods and statistical scales for sampling fish and fishery products. Formulated under the FAD 12 sectional committee, this standard unifies sampling protocols for canned, fresh, frozen, dried, and dry-salted fish, as well as fish oils, across India. It defines what constitutes a lot, establishes precise sampling tables (with sample sizes ranging from 2 up to 24 depending on lot volume), details aseptic collection of composite samples for microbiological testing, and enforces a strict testing timeline—requiring sampling within three weeks of delivery and testing within one week of collection.
